notes: Single commit, test-only change (internal/httpapi/integration_test.go): seed() queues statements into a pgx.Batch and flushes before every read-back; SQL text unchanged.

Verified flush ordering by reading the whole seed(): flush at :124 precedes the first QueryRow, every pool.QueryRow/pool.Exec between :127 and :395 only depends on rows inserted by earlier QueryRows or on rows already flushed at :382, and the derived-rollup INSERT...SELECTs (:351-:381) run inside the same batch after the raw_events inserts so they see them in the implicit transaction.
Error path: flush() drains results in queued order so the SQL reported on failure is the failing statement; results.Close() is called on both paths, no leak.

Ran the package myself against a throwaway postgres:16 container with -race: ok, 43s, 0 failures; only skip is the pre-existing opt-in TestEndpointLatencyUnderLoad (loadPool). TestTheFixtureIsWhatItSaysItIs passes. Fixture-only test on main's version of the file: 3.0s vs 0.29s on HEAD, which matches the commit message's numbers.

Behavioural difference worth knowing: inside one batch now() is a single transaction timestamp for all ~2000 statements (previously it advanced ~3s across autocommits). Nothing in the fixture or tests relies on that drift, and it removes a latent cross-midnight flake rather than adding one.

Commit message's last paragraph about CI runs not appearing on main pushes is commentary, not something this diff changes; ci.yml already sets MOMENTO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN and runs go test -race ./internal/..., so this change will be exercised there.
